title: The Combined Benefit Year Maximum Across Riders Held Together
content:
The Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are sold one to a member at a time but may be held together. Where a member holds more than one of them, what the riders pay between them in a benefit year is capped by one combined maximum as well as by each rider's own maximum.

## The order the two caps are taken in

Each rider's own annual maximum is applied first on its own claims; the combined cap then applies across the riders, and a line that would pass it is paid only up to what is left.

## What counts toward a maximum

What counts toward both maximums is what the riders actually paid, so a line denied or reversed uses none of the member's entitlement and a member whose claim was reversed gets that headroom back.

## Two riders reaching the same service

Where two riders could both pay for the same service, the rider whose benefit category names the service pays it, and the other pays nothing; the two are never added together for one line.

## The benefit year boundary

The combined cap resets with the benefit year and nothing carries forward, and a member close to it is told before they begin treatment rather than afterwards.

## Condition, judgement and result

| Condition | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A line falls within both the rider's own annual maximum and the combined cap | Both caps allow it | The line is paid on its own terms |
| A line would carry the riders past the combined cap | The combined cap governs | The line is paid only up to what is left of the combined cap |
| A line was denied, or has been reversed | Nothing was actually paid on it | It uses none of the entitlement under either maximum |
| A member holds two riders whose categories both reach one service | The rider whose benefit category names the service pays | That rider pays; the other pays nothing, and the two are not added |
